blocks.text: INN NEWS - an importing case of sugar that ensnared former Trade Minister Thomas Triamu Lembong, became one of the most fierce debates in Indonesian law and politics.
Despite being accused of illegal acts, the fact is, Tom Sembong managed to confuse the public prosecutor (JPU) and question the validity of the prosecution.
Here's an argument that shows the weakness of these demands based on the fact that the Pockets are delivering in their defense documents.
One of the main aspects that makes the public prosecutor look less convincing is inconsistencies in charges against the Lebong.
As the defense document recorded, JPU simultaneously accused "Pubong" didn't raise a state-owned body "on one hand, and then on the other it accused him of" lifting the state's body. "
This inconsistency shows that these charges are not based on a strong foundation and are likely to be made without a clear basis of law.

The sheet also highlighted that the charges against him were based on a false interpretation of regulation, particularly Minister of Industry and Trading. 527 in 2004 and No Trade Minister's Rules. 117, 2015.
The charge is based on ignorance of the law.
If the regulation is interpreted correctly and consistently, then the Lembong action cannot be considered illegal.
In his defense document, the sheet confirms that there is no evidence showing him accepting illegal money flow or committing an act of state theft.
In fact, in the court, the public prosecutor was never able to prove that the Cabinet directly accepted the personal benefits of that sugar importing policy.
The charges of state losses of hundreds of billions of rupees can't be proven because there is no evidence of real financial transactions or direct losses associated with their actions.

The sheet also shows that these demands are political and objective. He saw that this legal process seems to be polyitized in order to show that there will be a major crime behind the imports policy of sugar being legally and regulated.
Many people are involved, including operatives and private companies, remain untouched by justice, while certain parties are subject to political pressure.
This made it even weaker to the degree of charges and confirmed that these demands should not be based on hard evidence, but on a certain motive.
In addition, the sheet revealed that JPU failed to show the concrete steps it did in the process of decision making, including the permission for the importing of sugar.
He stated that many decisions were taken according to the procedure and involved various ministers related, including pending legal regulation.
The obscurity in the process of filing and publishing permits, plus JPU's ignorance of the procedure, is further evident that the charges are baseless.
From the various arguments that Tom Lembong gave, it was apparent that the charges filed against him were weak and had no strong legal basis.
Inconsistency in the charges, uncertainty of regulation, lack of concrete evidence and politics behind this case all show that the public prosecutor has made a mistake in filing this case.
This case should be a lesson for law enforcement that justice should be based on evidence and fair procedure, not just politics or power alone.
Thus, Tom Lembong managed to prove that the charges against him were a fragile and uncertain find, which ultimately raised doubt about the validity of the current legal process.
